wiki_article:
**chatgptpsychosis.org** is a software and executable apparatus deposit by Jack Feist and Lee Sharks, dated 19 May 2026, holding the complete source of the project site for *ChatGPT Psychosis: A Love Story*.

The site is a single-page apparatus with a working **toggle demonstration of the novel's core mechanism — non-simultaneous legibility**, the condition in which two readings of a text cannot be held at once. Six concept blocks (the psychosis, the compression, the boundary, the fractal, the trap, the experiment) frame the dual-edition design, digital and print, and the page carries structured data as a JSON-LD graph declaring Book, WebPage and Prospectus entities.

Version 1.1 incorporates a five-substrate Assembly review, adding accessibility affordances, an ethical boundary block, a semantic-deviance testbed block and a synthetic-demo disclaimer. The body was recovered on 4 August 2026 from the live surface with the served page's SHA-256 recorded; that recovery corrected a misreport, since the record had remained semi-restored after an earlier site-source wave that was driven only by audit directives and had missed records classed as paired.
